name: Imperial Novel route registry
scope: Source-audited Worker page-shell inventory. This registry certifies dispatcher-to-shell mapping only; it does not certify client rendering completeness, authorization, ownership isolation, locale/RTL behavior, canonical metadata, live HTTP status, or production deployment.
knownOpenQuestions: /fandom/:slug is a compatibility redirect, not a dedicated fandom landing.
/discover aliases /catalog; canonical metadata needs runtime verification.
/for-you aliases /made-for-you; canonical metadata needs runtime verification.
Shared discoveryPage renderers require per-feature functional and authorization tests.
HTTP method and object-level permissions are not certified by this UI route manifest.
Production status, active assets, cache behavior and browser navigation remain unverified.
Route-level authentication and role requirements must be reconciled against client navigation guards and API method/object authorization; this shell map does not certify them.
Per-route canonical URL, locale, RTL, and navigation exposure policies are not yet fully registered.
Dynamic novel/chapter sitemap eligibility is rights- and publication-filtered in the Worker; runtime sitemap output still needs integration tests.
Live Worker behavior, HTTP status codes, browser navigation, and deployed asset versions require runtime verification.

/omniportal is publicly linked and included in the static sitemap; external search is limited to enabled authorized connectors and imports require authentication plus an enabled authorized connector. Confirm whether a global product-level disable switch is required before treating the portal as fully off.

The route access policy is an initial source audit, not a full API/object authorization certification. In particular, reader chapter-content and unlock endpoints need a dedicated resource-ownership and entitlement review.

limitations: The Worker page shell is public even for routes whose client renderer later shows a sign-in or role-gated state.
Client checks improve navigation UX but are not security boundaries; API authorization and object ownership are authoritative.
The reader chapter-content, unlock, and per-object authorization path still needs a dedicated endpoint-to-resource audit.
Canonical URLs, locale negotiation, per-chapter RTL behavior, navigation exposure, and deployed runtime behavior remain separate unfinished registry dimensions.
